correctness.rationale: The stored checker reconstructs the exact (2,2,3) lattice graph (32 vertices, 41 edges), enumerates all 50 maximal perfect matchings by complete recursion and confirms the count separately by bipartite dynamic programming and MacMahon multiplication. It creates every one of 2,517,788 augmented simplicial faces and applies exact sequential element pairings on 41 edge labels. Exactly 1,258,893 pairs leave only two critical four-faces. A published rigorous theorem states that successive element pairings are acyclic. Forman Morse theory yields one zero-cell plus two four-cells, necessarily a wedge of two four-spheres. Control (2,2,2) matches the known 20 facets and 66,369 nonempty faces; the reduced Euler characteristic independently agrees. The argument is finite and does not extrapolate.

value.rationale: The article identifying the problem explicitly leaves honeycombs larger than (2,2,2) open. The (2,2,3) region is the smallest next three-side-length case and a natural nonsymmetric finite test of whether the sphere-wedge phenomenon extends. Its 2.5 million-face complex receives an exact integer homotopy classification, not a routine face or matching count. This motivated first new case is useful for discerning the potential family pattern without claiming a general result.
